skill.name: prototype
skill.description: Builds disposable logic or UI prototypes to test state models, data shapes, and interface directions before committing production code.
skill.summary: Create disposable prototypes that answer one design or logic question.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Design and state questions often stay unclear until users can try them. This skill creates throwaway logic or UI prototypes that expose decisions quickly.
actual_capabilities: Chooses between logic and UI prototype paths based on the user question.
Builds small interactive terminal prototypes for state models and reducers.
Creates multiple UI variants behind a shareable ?variant= switcher.
Uses existing project tooling and routing instead of adding a new stack.
Captures prototype results in notes, issues, ADRs, or commit messages.
limitations: Prototype code is disposable and not ready for production without cleanup.
It does not add full tests, robust error handling, or long-term abstractions.
It depends on the host project runtime and component patterns.
It may need user input when the design question is ambiguous.

use_cases.title: Validate a State Model
use_cases.description: Create a small terminal prototype that exposes transitions, invalid actions, and current state for manual review.

use_cases.title: Compare UI Directions
use_cases.description: Build several structurally different variants on a real route, using existing data and layout context.

use_cases.title: De-Risk a Workflow Change
use_cases.description: Test a workflow idea before the team commits to architecture, tickets, or production implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Prototype a State Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a tiny logic prototype for this state question: [describe state and edge case]. Use the existing project runtime.

prompt_templates.title: Compare UI Directions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three UI variants for [page or component]. Keep the current data and route, and make each variant structurally different.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Complex Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a throwaway prototype for [workflow]. Expose each state transition, invalid action, and result so we can review the model by hand.

prompt_templates.title: Capture the Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the prototype results for [question]. Recommend which parts to keep, what to rewrite, and what files to delete.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether a billing retry state machine handles expired cards and manual payments.
output: A runnable logic prototype with visible current state after each action.
A short run command using existing tooling.
A notes file recording tested edge cases and the observed answer.

output_examples.input: A team wants options for a settings page redesign.
output: Three visually distinct variants on the existing route.
A bottom switcher that preserves the selected variant in the URL.
A cleanup note explaining which variant won.

output_examples.input: A lead wants to validate a new onboarding flow before planning implementation.
output: A focused prototype for the key workflow decisions.
Visible state or screen variants for fast review.
A concise decision record for the next implementation step.

best_practices: State the single question before writing prototype code.
Keep prototype logic separate from throwaway display or switcher code.
Delete losing variants and record the decision when the prototype is done.
anti_patterns: Do not promote prototype code directly to production.
Do not add new tooling when the project already has a runtime.
Do not connect prototypes to real mutations unless persistence is the question.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a design, state, or workflow question needs a quick working prototype before production work starts.

faq.question: Does this skill create production code?
faq.answer: No. It creates disposable prototype code that should be deleted or rewritten after the decision is clear.

faq.question: Can it work with existing app routes?
faq.answer: Yes. For UI work, it prefers existing routes so variants use real data and realistic page context.

faq.question: Can it help with backend logic?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build small terminal prototypes for reducers, state machines, data shapes, and workflow rules.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is prepared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should happen after the prototype answers the question?
faq.answer: Record the decision, keep only validated ideas, and remove the throwaway prototype files.
